<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **48** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23419bafb742fc13fa3c22b446263bbd6041c78e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `49c16919862432de9263d42db4d67f02d5334c6d` — the merge of head `1e13bb28fcb63bc5d73fa546b5c75c032957ad0e` into base `23419bafb742fc13fa3c22b446263bbd6041c78e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 49c16919862432de9263d42db4d67f02d5334c6d && git checkout 49c16919862432de9263d42db4d67f02d5334c6d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 23419bafb742fc13fa3c22b446263bbd6041c78e 1e13bb28fcb63bc5d73fa546b5c75c032957ad0e && git checkout -B drift-repro 23419bafb742fc13fa3c22b446263bbd6041c78e && git merge --no-ff 1e13bb28fcb63bc5d73fa546b5c75c032957ad0e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23419bafb742fc13fa3c22b446263bbd6041c78e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 23419bafb742fc13fa3c22b446263bbd6041c78e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bf3f89075e9f45ef9cc81e8de6f43d6620ea5127`
Local-runs: none

Stage 2d of #15204 (claim amendment 6106681412, dispatched from F5 of objectui#12089 round 2; dev report 6107337287). Read on GitHub only: the card body and all 88 comments (the 2c records 6104861792 and 6105494730 on #22736, the 2c Landed 6105781131, the stage-1 ACCEPT 6102862135 and the rulings among them), objectui comment 6106225321 (F5, the measured defect) and the seat note 6106420299 on objectui#7611, the PR body, its 9-file list (+341 / −30), the net diff against `main`, and the 35 check-runs on this head. `main` was read for every reader and writer of `sys_metadata_activation.package_id`: the shared store and the object, the catalog door and the action door, objectql's `action-activation.ts` and `engine.ts`, service-automation's `flow-activation-store.ts` and `engine.ts` (the toggle and the hydrator), core's `resolve-authz-context.ts` and `security-catalog.ts`, plugin-auth's `last-admin-guard.ts`, the CLI's ownership inventory and unmanaged-tables readers, the route ledger, `http-dispatcher.ts`, `@objectstack/types`' `thrown-http-error.ts` and `validation-failure.ts`, the two docs pages, and ADR-0112, ADR-0113, ADR-0126 §4 and ADR-0131 D3/D6/D7.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **What the door now accepts — right, and it is the accept set 2c already declared.** 2c's PASS (6104861792 ①.3) judged the door's name space as the catalog reader's: registry first, then the metadata service. An item saved through `PUT /meta/position/:name` or `PUT /meta/permission/:name` was therefore in the declared accept set from the start; F5 is that step 5 (the ledger write) refused what step 4 (the declaration) admitted. On this head steps 1 to 4 are unchanged hunks: both authority gates, the shape 400, the anchors' 400 in both directions, the shared body reader, the 404, the no-reader and reader-throws 503s and the no-ledger 501. Only the write and its `catch` move. So `POST /api/v1/security/_activation/:type/:name` widens to nothing 2c's record did not already cover; it is made to hold. The row the door passes is right by construction: `SecurityCatalogEntry.packageId` is the definition's `_packageId` only when that is a non-empty string (`ownerOf`, `security-catalog.ts`), so the door can never hand the store `''`, and the spread passes a packaged item's package verbatim (the `crm` control pins it).

2. **`package_id` no longer `required` — right, and what an empty value means to every reader.** ADR-0113: `required` is a write-time check; the column constraint is `storage.notNull` (`schema-drift.ts` compares nullability against `field.storage?.notNull`, and the DDL keys off the same knob), and this field declares none, so the column was nullable on disk, no DDL, no migration. The readers, each read on `main`:
   - `readDisabledCatalogNames` (`core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:780`): one `$in` read by `metadata_type` and `name`, then `active === false || active === 0`. `package_id` is not read. A package-less row that is off is disabled exactly like a packaged one; it cannot read as "no row", because the row is selected by key.
   - `ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore.list()`: its only consumers are `hydrateFlowActivations` (service-automation `engine.ts:5028`) and `ActionActivationProjection.hydrate` (objectql), and both read `name` and `active` only.
   - plugin-auth's ledger hooks `guardActivationLedgerInsert` / `guardActivationLedgerUpdate` (`last-admin-guard.ts:1637`): standing is keyed by type, name and `active`.
   - the flow toggle (`engine.ts:5694`) and the action door are writers only; neither reads a row back.
   - CLI: `organization-ownership-inventory.ts:268` lists the ledger as `column-drop` for the tenant column and reads no `package_id` (the `groupBy ['type','name','package_id']` at :317 is the `sys_metadata` entry); `unmanaged-tables.ts` reads no column.
   - Setup's object list shows `package_id` through `highlightFields` and renders blank; the console's own ledger read is the data door's list by name (F5's measurement). The dev's objectui census (no `package_id` reader at `a194b4e`) is outside this brief's inputs and is recorded as the dev's measurement.
   No reader compares a row's package with anything, so no reader can take a package-less row for a packaged one; every reader keys by `(metadata_type, name)` and reads `active`, so none can take it for "no row". Row identity stays the `'global'` index over the two key columns, untouched.

3. **One spelling for "no package" — right, with one inert tolerance.** `setActive` writes `null` when `packageId` is absent and refuses `''` with a `TypeError` before the keyed `find` (pinned: zero engine calls). `list()` returns `packageId` only for a non-empty string. The extra `!== ''` arm on the read is a dead branch: no writer produces `''` (the store refuses it; before this head `required` refused it; the flow store always names the loader's package), so it tolerates a spelling that cannot be on disk. Noted, not a defect.

4. **The public types.** `MetadataActivationRow.packageId?` (`@objectstack/core`, `export *` from `utils/metadata-activation-store.js`) and `FlowActivationRow.packageId?` (`@objectstack/service-automation`, `index.ts:36`). The second is forced by the first: `ObjectStoreFlowActivationStore extends ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore implements FlowActivationStore`, so `list()`'s row type must admit the shared row (the dev's reverse check: 10 × TS2345). objectql's `ActionActivationRow = MetadataActivationRow` is an alias and follows with no edit, which is why the typecheck of objectql is green with nothing changed there. A consumer that read `packageId` as `string` loses a type guarantee; no reader in the repo did, and the changeset states FROM → TO.

5. **The `catch` moving to `deps.errorFromThrown(err, 503)` — right; every refusal now keeps ADR-0112's pair.** `HttpDispatcher.errorFromThrown` is `resolveThrownHttpError` (`@objectstack/types`) plus the 5xx leak withhold. Its precedence: status = `.status` → `.statusCode` → 400 when the throw is a validation shape → the fallback; code = `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a validation shape → a ledger-registered `.code` → the code the status derives; an unregistered `.code` demotes to `declaredCode`. Applied to this door's three throws:
   - the last-admin guard: `refuse()` sets `code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED'` and `status: 403`, so the pair is 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, unchanged, and the 4xx message reaches the caller intact;
   - the engine's record `ValidationError` (`code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'`, `fields[]`, no status): 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`, and `details.fields` now reaches the wire, which the old `catch` dropped. Pinned in the unit test through the real `HttpDispatcher`, and the dev's ablation showed the same pair with `fields[package_id required]` on a real engine;
   - a bare store failure: 503, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` derived from the status, the message withheld when it looks like a leak, which is what the old `deps.error(message, 503, { code })` path did too; the existing pin still passes.
   The anchors' 400, the unknown-name 404, the no-reader 503 and the no-ledger 501 are `deps.error` calls above the `try` and do not move.

6. **The published text.** `authorization.mdx`: every added sentence is true of the code (the package recorded when there is one and `package_id` left empty when none; both honoured because the resolver keys by type and name; 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a record validation failure; a hook's pair kept; 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` for a store failure). The object file gains a true paragraph and a true field description. Nit, same file: the object's `description` ("Activation ledger for packaged metadata artifacts … one row per packaged artifact") and the `name` and `active` descriptions ("The packaged artifact's machine name", "Is the packaged artifact armed") still say "packaged" while `package_id`'s says otherwise; those strings are served through `/meta` and Setup. Follow-up push.

7. **ADR alignment, stated.** ADR-0126 §4's table types `package_id` as "the package that ships the base artifact"; ADR-0131 D6 frames regime C's bit as a managed item's; D7's parity note says an environment-authored set's `active` "moves into the environment-authored definition's lifecycle, since there is no row". On `main` the resolver reads no definition lifecycle for these two types, only the ledger (`resolve-authz-context.ts` 6a), so before this head an environment-authored position or set had no working switch at all. #22621 → A, as the seat note 6106420299 and the 2c Landed record restate it, has the platform administrator switching environment-authored items from Setup through this door. The ADR prose is now narrower than `main`; the carrier for that text is the cutover's ADR note (#22619, Tier H; D14's execution-plan note already names #22621), not this PR.

8. **Exclusions, scope, merge.** No transition piece (no row fallback, no junction read, no write-through). No change to who may write the catalog. Nothing under `content/docs/releases/`. Nine files: four source, three tests, one changeset, one docs page; `service-automation/src/engine.ts` is the one file outside the declared zone, type only, forced as ①.4 says. The merge commit `bf3f8907` brings `main` in and adds no file of another stage; GitHub reports the PR mergeable and clean.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/15204-catalog-activation-environment-authored.md`: `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, each **minor**; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on its own line, the same line as the PR body's second line (AGENTS.md: `yes|no` plus at most one arm from the closed pair; `yes` takes at least minor). Right per package: runtime (the door's declared accept set now holds for environment-authored items; a record validation refusal moves 503 → 400, a status correction on a refusal, no removal); core (an optional property, and `''` refused — `''` never landed before either, so no end-to-end accept set shrinks); platform-objects (`required` dropped, an object-schema widening); service-automation (type only). `@objectstack/dogfood` is private; the docs page is repo-owned. No ADR-0087 marker is owed (no `packages/spec` disposition) and none is present. `Check Changeset` is green.
- **One wording defect.** The last bullet is headed "**Not changed: the action activation door**" and then states that its answer moves from 503 `VALIDATION_FAILED` to 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. The door's code is unchanged; its published answer is not, and the body says so. A CHANGELOG heading that reads "not changed" over a described change misleads the reader the body is written for. The heading must say what the body says (③.2). Fix it in the follow-up push on this PR, before any Version Packages PR carries it.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Open question 1, (i) or (ii) → A/(i), as built.** No reader reads `package_id` (①.2), so a marker string would serve nobody and put a second dialect into a provenance column; `null` says what is true.
2. **Open question 2, the action door — answered on `main`, and the carrier corrected.** Traced: `handleActionActivationWrite` (`runtime/src/domains/actions.ts:223`) passes `String(_packageId ?? '')` to `ql.setActionActive`, which is a pass-through (objectql `engine.ts:5217`) to `ActionActivationProjection.setActive`, whose store is `ObjectStoreActionActivationStore`, a one-argument binding of the core store. So for an action no package ships the new `TypeError` is thrown there and the action door's own `catch` answers 503 with `code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'` and the store's sentence. Before this head the same request answered 503 `VALIDATION_FAILED` "Package is required" (the engine's refusal under the door's wrong default status). Judgments: (a) **it is a changed published answer** of `POST /api/v1/actions/_activation/:object/:action`, and the changeset must state it as a change, not under "Not changed"; the new answer's message ("Omit packageId for an item no package ships") addresses a TypeScript caller and is served to an HTTP client, under a code whose semantics are a retryable outage for a refusal no retry clears; (b) **in scope: the cause, not the fix.** The cause is this PR's store refusal; the fix is in `actions.ts`, outside 2d's declared files, and the action door's own docblock declares "it does not require the action to be PACKAGED … a row for a runtime-authored artifact is harmless", a capability `main` has never delivered (refused by `required` before this head, by the store after it). Whether an environment-authored action gets a switch or a deliberate 4xx refusal is a product question #22621 does not reach; (c) **the right carrier is a filed card, not "none".** Prime Directive #10 files a contract violation (declared, not enforced) rather than noting it; the dev's `carrier: none` is the wrong placement. **Escalated to the seat:** file the card (an environment-authored action through the action door: open the switch, or refuse it with a 4xx pair and a sentence; either way the `?? ''` goes), and have the follow-up push rename the bullet. Not a FAIL reason: the door's answer for this request class was already a contradicting pair before this head, nothing lands either way, nothing newly reachable opens, the pair now agrees with itself, and `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` documents the action switch for packaged actions only, so no published page is falsified.
3. **Deviation: the objectui comments unread by the dev.** Both are this record's inputs. F5's measured defect (`POST /api/v1/security/_activation/permission/c9_r2_env_set` → 503 `{ code: VALIDATION_FAILED, message: 'Package is required', httpStatus: 503 }`, and the same for `position/c9_r2_registry_only` in both directions, on objectstack `490cb6d9`) is exactly what the dev reproduced on `9f5eca5` and what this diff fixes. The seat note's reading of the seam (the door's `?? ''` against the field's `required: true`, and the `catch`'s 503 default) matches the diff's two moves. Closed.
4. **Deviation: `engine.ts` outside the zone** — right (①.4), and the changeset names the package.
5. **Deviation: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`** — well-formed under AGENTS.md's declaration shape.
6. **The in-memory double is now more lenient than the store it stands for.** `InMemoryMetadataActivationStore.setActive` (and so the flow and action in-memory bindings) accepts `''`. No test on `main` pins `''` through it (the action-dispatch and store tests name no empty package), so nothing is wrong today; carrier: the same change that drops the action door's `?? ''`, or a one-line refusal in the double. Not blocking.
7. **Docs inside the diff's own file** (①.6): the three "packaged" strings on the object. Follow-up push.
8. **Dogfood test hygiene.** The new case saves two `/meta` items, signs a holder up and inserts a `sys_user_position` row that the file's `afterAll` does not remove; that is the base file's own posture (`usp_catalog_activation_exec`), and the three Dogfood Regression Gate shards and their roll-up are green on this head.
9. **Release-cut condition (a)** of 6102862135, extended to 2d by 6106681412 and the seat note: met when this head lands. Landing per the amendment: on this PASS.
10. **Check-runs on this head, all complete: 35 runs, 33 `success`, 2 roster skips (Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)), 0 `failure`.** Green: all six `Test Core` shards and the roll-up, the three `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards and the roll-up, Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint & Repo Gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, the four Type Check gates and TypeScript Type Check, Spec property liveness, Temporal Conformance, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label, and the five PR-form gates. No red is left to attribute.
